Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the HealthBridge Hospitals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone and wait for further instructions. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HealthBridge Hospitals' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.  

Dr. Michael Reynolds:  
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.  

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on four key aspects: total admissions and patient days, the impact of recent acquisitions on our performance, the effects of our value-based care contracts on reimbursement, and the factors driving our operating margin expansion.  

On volumes, we saw robust growth in both admissions and patient days, reflecting strong demand and effective capacity management. Our recent acquisitions have already delivered meaningful revenue contributions and synergies, strengthening our footprint in high-growth markets. Value-based care initiatives are enhancing our reimbursement profile through shared savings and quality incentives. And overall, these elements combined to deliver impressive margin performance.  

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Jennifer to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.  

Jennifer Lee:  
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Reynolds mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter was $2.45 billion, an increase of 9.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume and improved payer mix.  

Our operating expenses were $2.14 billion, representing 87.2% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives.  

Net income for the quarter was $250 million, or $2.08 per diluted share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.  

To expand on the key aspects Dr. Reynolds highlighted, let me start with our core volume metrics: total admissions and patient days, with both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter comparisons. These are foundational to our revenue momentum, showcasing patient demand alongside our sharp operational focus despite challenges like labor constraints, evolving payer dynamics, and the ongoing move to outpatient settings.  

For Q2 ended June 30, 2024, we achieved total admissions of 287,500, marking a 2.1% increase from 281,400 in Q1 and a 5.3% rise from 273,100 in Q2 2023. Patient days totaled 1.78 million, up 1.2% sequentially from 1.76 million in Q1 and ahead 4.8% year-over-year from 1.70 million. This resulted in an average length of stay of 6.19 days, holding steady quarter-over-quarter from 6.25 days and edging up 10 basis points annually, thanks to a shift toward more complex cases.  

Breaking it down further, inpatient admissions—our core strength—climbed 2.5% quarter-over-quarter and 6.1% year-over-year to 215,000, propelled by renewed elective activity in orthopedics and cardiology. Observation stays rose 1.8% sequentially to 72,500, tied to seasonal upticks in respiratory cases from late-spring RSV and early flu trends. Adjusted patient days, incorporating our 0.56 outpatient factor consistent with peers like HCA Healthcare, reached 2.92 million, gaining 1.7% from Q1 and 6.2% from last year—a clear sign of rising acuity and better utilization.  

Our average daily census hit 19,778 occupied beds, improving from 19,530 in Q1, with occupancy at a steady 68%, matching benchmarks from Community Health Systems and Tenet Healthcare amid tight capacity. Case mix index advanced to 1.72, a 2% year-over-year gain, boosted by emphasis on high-acuity lines where surgical volumes surged 8% annually, supported by our da Vinci Xi systems now numbering 150 across our 45 hospitals.  

Sequentially, growth faced typical Q1-to-Q2 softness from spring scheduling dips, but we beat expectations via our value-based care network with UnitedHealthcare's Optum, lifting bundled admissions 3.5% quarter-over-quarter, especially in joints and heart failure. New inpatient rehab facilities in the Southeast added 4% to patient days, mirroring Select Medical's approach with three sites launched since late last year.  

Year-over-year, we outran the 3-4% sector norm per Definitive Healthcare, with broad gains: medical admissions up 4.2% on oncology and behavioral health surges amid mental health needs, surgical up 7.1%, and women's services up 5.8% from OB/GYN buildouts. Patient days trailed slightly due to payer pressure on discharges, but CMI lifts countered that, enhancing revenue per case by 6%.  

By region, Sunbelt areas—Texas, Florida, Arizona, 55% of beds—excelled with 7.2% admissions growth and 6.5% on days, aided by inflows and stable uninsured rates post-Medicaid adjustments. Texas led at 9%, akin to Tenet's Conifer sites, via Houston expansions. Northeast (New York, Pennsylvania; 20% beds) managed 2.1% admissions growth against regulatory hurdles and denials from Empire BlueCross, but days rose 4% on acuity. Midwest (25% beds) posted even 5% growth, buffered by solid Blue Cross ties.  

These results highlight our high-acuity, high-efficiency approach. Year-to-date digital health spend of $250 million, including Epic MyChart at 80% of sites, sped admissions 12% with AI bed tools like Cleveland Clinic's. Tele-ICU with Philips added 15,000 days sans new capital. Our Q1 short-stay hospital buy added 1,200 admissions in Q2, hitting 75% synergy goals.  

Ahead, we see Q3 admissions up 4-6% year-over-year on electives and 500-bed pipeline, tempered by Gulf hurricane risks. Days at 4-5%, ALOS firm as ASCs—five opened year-to-date—shift 10% low-acuity cases. These trends fuel margins in a field where scale and tech prevail.  

Next, let's discuss the impact of our recent acquisitions on financial performance. Earlier this year, we closed two key deals: the $1.2 billion acquisition of Southeast Regional Hospitals, a 1,200-bed acute network in Georgia, Florida, and the Carolinas, and the $450 million purchase of Ambulatory Care Innovators, operator of 45 outpatient surgery and imaging centers in dense markets like Atlanta, Dallas, and Phoenix. These were EPS-accretive from day one, adding $0.28 to adjusted earnings in Q2, with full-year upside of $1.10 per share.  

Pro forma for the full quarter, they generated $285 million in net revenue, or 12% of our $2.45 billion total, which grew 22% year-over-year adjusted. SRH contributed $210 million from inpatient and outpatient, with surgical cases up 12%, especially complex ortho and cardio. SRH's CMI rose to 1.85 from 1.72 pre-deal, aided by commercial mix at 52% versus 45%, following renegotiations with Blues and UnitedHealthcare. ACI brought $75 million, with 15% same-site procedure growth in premium ASC work like cataracts, scopes, and injections, yielding over 35% EBITDA margins.  

Ex-acquisitions, same-facility revenue rose 5.2%, amplified by synergies: $32 million run-rate savings year-to-date, 85% toward our $45 million Year 1 goal. Supply chain yielded $18 million via Vizient GPO standardization on implants and drugs, saving 12-15%. Back-office added $10 million through Workday HRIS and shared RCM. Clinical tweaks cut ALOS 0.4 days to 4.2 system-wide, for $4 million.  

Margins benefited too: Q2 adjusted EBITDA at $313 million, or 12.8%, up 210 basis points year-over-year. Deals added 150 basis points pro forma. SRH margins climbed from 14.2% to 16.8% on 8% day growth and staffing efficiencies benchmarking USPI and SCA. ACI shone at 32%. Integration costs were $22 million, mostly Epic IT for 75% SRH beds, tapering to $15 million in Q3.  

Operationally, acquisition admissions grew 11% year-over-year, topping AHA's 4.1% national trend, strong in Sunbelt with MA at 45% up from 38%. We shifted 25,000 SRH patients to ACO REACH, aiming 3-5% readmission cuts via Encompass and LHC ties. Outpatient now 28% of procedures via ACI, grabbing 20% more commercial amid CMS OPPS cuts.  

Southeast is transformative: Florida/Georgia grow 2.5x population via migration and seniors (22% new patients over 65). Added three da Vinci suites at SRH, lifting procedural margins 400 basis points. ACI in Texas/Arizona rides ambulatory wave; Phoenix up 18% against COVID backlogs.  

This builds our hub-and-spoke model, linking hospitals to ASCs/imaging for full care episodes, like Tenet with Conifer/USPI but tech-forward: Palantir Foundry AI now across assets predicts no-shows at 92% accuracy, block utilization at 88%, priming MSSP and BPCI wins.  

Forward, Q3 synergies at $12 million, full-year EBITDA add $95 million, ROIC over 12% by 2026. Labor risks—14% turnover in acquired vs. 10% core—eased by bonuses and traveler cuts. Integration 70% done, full Epic by year-end. These moves accelerate growth in consolidation, powering payer leverage and tech.  

Shifting to the impact of value-based care contracts on our reimbursement. This is a major driver of stability and margins as we transition from fee-for-service. Our VBC contracts now cover 42% of net patient revenue, up from 32% last year and 38% in Q1, spanning MSSP Track 3 ACOs for 150,000 lives in our 12-hospital Southeast/Midwest cluster, MA upside/two-sided risk with Humana and UnitedHealthcare, commercial VBC with Blues in Georgia/Tennessee, and BPCI Advanced bundles for 15% of ortho/cardiac electives.  

Reimbursement impact is positive, despite investments. FFS averaged $14,200 per discharge on 1.85 CMI and ASP tweaks, but VBC PMPM hit $850, 8% above FFS peers, via bonuses and savings. H1 shared savings reached $28 million net of 20% withholds, up 56% from $18 million last year, on 4.2% TCOC cuts.  

Quality is key: 92nd percentile CMS Stars for MA earned full 5.5% QIPs. Readmissions for AMI/HF/PN fell to 14.8% from 16.2%, beating 15.9% national, dodging full HRRP penalties. HCAHPS at 4.1 stars backs NPS-tied commercial bonuses.  

Regionally, Georgia/Florida (MA >45%) show 12% VBC premium over FFS; Tampa at 65% VBC mix hits 10% EBITDA vs. 7% overall. Rural Tennessee lags at 25% VBC but Optum EOCV sepsis pilot saves 7% TCOC, eyeing $5 million FY24 upside.  

Tech investments: $45 million Epic MyChart with Google Cloud API cut denials 22%, risk-stratified via AI. Summit Care Pathways flags CHF risks, cuts readmits 18%, unlocks $12 million MSSP YTD. Amedisys SNF networks trimmed ALOS 0.8 days, VBC margins to 11.5% from 9.2%.  

We're ahead: McKinsey sees VBC at 55% payments by 2026 from 36%, CMS 100% risk by 2030. HCA at 30% VBC had flat margins; Tenet Conifer faces downside. Our hedge—15% at full cap risk—plus 3:1 ROI on pop health including SDOH workers.  

Challenges: Part D drug redesign cut PMPM 1.5%; payers narrow networks. Countered by mix (Medicare 52%, MA 18%, commercial 25%) and HHS-HCC v28 advocacy. VBC added 220 bps to revenue per admission, fueling 350 bps EBITDA expansion. FY25 growth 60% from VBC, $75-90 million savings.  

Finally, tying it together, the factors affecting our operating margin, which hit 12.8%—up 210 basis points from 10.7% in Q2 2023, our best since pre-pandemic and outperforming HCA and Tenet. This stems from disciplined revenue levers and cost controls across our 45-hospital Southeast, Midwest, and Sunbelt network.  

Revenue grew 9.2% to $2.45 billion on 6.1% adjusted patient days, 4.8% admissions, 12% outpatient encounters—elective ortho/cardio rebound. CMI to 1.92 from 1.87 adds 150 bps per case via cardio/oncology. Commercial at 58% from 55%, 4.2% rate hikes with Blues/United; MA at 22% (85% FFS rates) offset by VBC pilots like Cleveland Clinic's, $18 million YTD savings on 15% readmit cuts via CareBridge telehealth/Epic.  

Southeast (25 hospitals, FL/GA/TX) up 11% revenue on inflows/low regs; Midwest softer at 5% from flu/Medicaid unwind (8% uncompensated in OH/IL). Q1 divestitures freed $150 million for ASCs at 20%+ margins.  

Costs rose 6.8% vs. industry inflation: labor (52% revenue) up 5.2% < peers' 7-9%, via Cerner RevElate AI scheduling (12% nurse productivity, 22% OT cut). Contract labor to 3.5% from 8%, $45 million sequential save; turnover 14% vs. 20% NSI avg via bonuses/Bridge to Excellence academy.  

Supplies up 4.1% vs. 7% sector (GLP-1 shortages), Vizient GPO saved 15% ortho/10% pharma. McKesson blockchain pilot eyes $30 million annual via pricing/inventory amid 25% endocrine inflation. Other ops +3%, AI-Palantir denial tool reversed $22 million, A/R to 42 from 48 days; bad debt 3.2% from 3.8% via charity.  

Ahead, 12-14% FY24 margins via 10 ASCs (25% revenue by 2026 like HCA), Pfizer CAR-T for CMI/diversification. Risks: SEIU wages, CMS IPPS cuts; but 2.8x leverage enables rural M&A. Revenue/volumes/costs delivered the beat; raising FY adj EBITDA/share to $10.25-$10.50.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Reynolds.  

Dr. Michael Reynolds:  
Thank you, Jennifer. At this time, we will open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.  

John Smith:  
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of Medicare Advantage reimbursement changes on your operations?  

Dr. Michael Reynolds:  
Good morning, John. Absolutely, MA shifts are a key focus. As Jennifer noted, penetration is at 22%, with rates around 85% of fee-for-service, which presents some pressure, but we've offset it effectively through our value-based pilots generating $18 million in shared savings year-to-date. In high-MA markets like Florida and Georgia, where it exceeds 45%, our VBC mix hits 65%, delivering a 12% reimbursement premium and 10% EBITDA margins there. Quality scores in the 92nd percentile secure full incentives, and tech like our AI pathways cut readmissions 18%, unlocking more upside. We're hedged with only 15% at full risk and diversified mix, positioning us well as CMS pushes toward 100% risk models.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.  

Lisa Chen:  
What are your expectations for patient volume growth in the next quarter, considering the current environment?  

Jennifer Lee:  
Thanks, Lisa. We're guiding Q3 admissions to 4-6% year-over-year growth, with patient days at 4-5%, building on Q2's 5.3% and 4.8% respectively. This assumes continued elective rebound and our 500-bed expansion, plus VBC bundles adding momentum, though we're watchful on seasonal flu and Gulf weather. ASC diversions help stabilize ALOS, and Sunbelt strength—Texas up 9% this year—should lead. Overall, tech like AI bed management and tele-ICU supports throughput without strain.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.  

Mike Patel:  
Thanks. On cost controls, how are you managing supply chain pressures, especially with drug shortages?  

Jennifer Lee:  
Great question, Mike. Supplies grew just 4.1% here versus 7% industry-wide, thanks to Vizient GPO savings of 15% on ortho and 10% on pharma, plus our McKesson blockchain pilot for real-time pricing and just-in-time stock—projecting $30 million annual savings amid Ozempic/Mounjaro hikes of 25%. Labor's contained too at 5.2% growth via AI scheduling boosting productivity 12% and contract use down to 3.5%. These keep us ahead of peers.  

Operator:  
[Operator Instructions] There are no further questions at this time.  

Dr. Michael Reynolds:  
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the HealthBridge Hospitals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
